claims.text: Russian President Vladimir Putin landed in New Delhi to attend the BRICS summit and hold a bilateral meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in India on early Friday ahead of the BRICS Summit 2026.
The BRICS Summit 2026 marks Vladimir Putin's first overseas participation in a BRICS summit since Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Russian President Vladimir Putin previously met on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Bishkek on August 31.
Russian presidential spokesperson Dmitry Peskov stated that Russia and India are exploring cooperation in rare earths and the possible sale of Sukhoi Su-57 stealth fighter jets to India.

Union Civil Aviation Minister Kinjarapu Ram Mohan Naidu confirmed that India and Russia have stepped up talks on manufacturing aircraft in India, including the IL-114 turboprop and Sukhoi Superjet 100.
Special airspace restrictions apply from September 11 to September 13 within a 300-km radius of New Delhi for the BRICS Summit.
Normal scheduled commercial flights at Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport will continue to take off and land during the BRICS Summit.
Nearly 4,800 traffic personnel have been deployed in Delhi for security and traffic management during the summit.
Safdarjung Airport will remain closed during the security period, except for specified IAF and BSF helicopter operations.
Aircraft climbing near the restricted zone around Delhi must reach Flight Level 290, around 29,000 feet, by the time they are 200 km from the capital.
The 18th BRICS summit is being hosted at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi.

Chinese President Xi Jinping, Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, Ethiopia's Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed Ali, and Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto are among the leaders expected to attend the BRICS summit in New Delhi.
UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, WHO head Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, and WTO Director-General Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala are scheduled to attend the BRICS summit.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian is scheduled to attend the summit, marking his first visit to India since taking office after President Ebrahim Raisi died in a helicopter crash in 2024.
Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Humayun Kobir confirmed that Bangladesh will not be represented at the summit despite an invitation to Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.
Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal stated India and Russia aim to reach target goals of $100 billion in bilateral trade and $50 billion in two-way investment by 2030.
Bilateral trade between India and Russia currently stands at around $60 billion.
The BRICS Summit 2026 takes place in New Delhi from September 12-13 under the theme 'Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability'.
Satya Niketan PG operator Shubham Tyagi was denied anticipatory bail by a Delhi court following a building collapse.
The Municipal Corporation of Delhi sealed at least 56 jewellery and bullion-related shops in Chandni Chowk's Kucha Mahajani on Thursday.
The MCD enforcement drive was intensified following a fatal building collapse in Satya Niketan on September 6 that left seven people dead.

The All India Bullion and Jewellers Association questioned whether, after the Satya Niketan tragedy, only traders will bear the brunt or if action will also be taken against government departments and politicians.
A five-storey paying guest building collapsed in Delhi's Satya Niketan on September 6, killing seven people and injuring 12.
Five of the seven people killed in the Satya Niketan PG building collapse were Delhi University students.
Initial findings revealed the collapsed 50-year-old building in Satya Niketan had five floors despite only two floors being permitted.
Police arrested the owner of the collapsed Satya Niketan building, his son, the operator, and a contractor.
The Municipal Corporation of Delhi suspended five municipal officials over alleged negligence related to the Satya Niketan collapse.
A Supreme Court Bench of Justices Ahsanuddin Amanullah and R Mahadevan directed authorities across India to file affidavits on compliance with directions regarding unauthorized constructions.
Amicus curiae Ajit Kumar Sinha brought the Satya Niketan building collapse in Motibagh to the Supreme Court's attention.
The Delhi High Court scheduled further hearings on the public interest litigation regarding the Satya Niketan incident for September 25.
Three additional engineers were suspended for negligence following the Delhi building collapse.
